report.tagline: The world's most used map app, for directions, traffic, finding places and checking reviews, now with Gemini AI to answer questions about where to go.
report.simpleSummary: Google Maps shows you where you are and how to get somewhere by car, bike, bus, metro or on foot, with live traffic. You can also search for a restaurant, a petrol pump or a doctor, read reviews, see photos and call or book. In 2026 Google added Ask Maps, where you type a question like 'a cafe near me with short lines and a charging point' and Gemini answers. Maps is free, and Google earns from businesses that pay for ads and from developers who pay to use Maps in their apps.

overview.whatItDoes: Google Maps is a free map, navigation and local search app on Android, iPhone, the web and cars. It gives turn-by-turn directions with live traffic, public transport routes, and a directory of places with reviews. Businesses list themselves for free through a Google Business Profile, and pay for ads to appear higher.
howItWorks: Google builds maps from satellite images, Street View cars, government data and user edits.
Phones running Maps share anonymous location speeds, which powers live traffic and arrival times.
Users search for places; results mix free Business Profiles with paid promoted pins and ads.
Users add reviews, photos and ratings, which help others choose and keep data fresh.
Developers like Uber, Zomato or Swiggy-style apps pay for the Maps Platform APIs for maps, routes and place data.
Gemini powers Ask Maps and Immersive Navigation, a 3D driving view with route pros and cons.
overview.valueProposition: For users: get anywhere and find anything nearby, free, with live traffic. For businesses: be found by people who are nearby and ready to visit.

businessModel.summary: Google Maps is free to users. It makes money from local businesses that pay for ads in Maps and Search, from developers who pay to use Maps data in their apps, and indirectly by feeding location knowledge into Google Search ads.

revenueStreams.detail: Promoted pins and ads in Maps search results, paid per click or action like a call or direction request.
Developers pay per map load, route or place request after a free tier.
Local results and place data make Search ads more valuable.
Google built-in maps in cars from carmakers.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Business Profiles are free. Ads are bought through Google Ads on a pay-per-click or pay-per-action basis. Maps Platform charges per request after free monthly usage; Google cut API prices in India in 2024 after Ola Maps launched a cheaper rival.
costDrivers: Servers for routing billions of trips
businessModel.unitEconomics: Think of one restaurant in Pune that pays ₹10,000 a month for local ads. If each click or direction request costs around ₹10 to ₹20, it gets 500 to 1,000 high-intent actions. Google's extra cost to show those ads is tiny because Maps is already built. Most of the value is from users who search 'near me' and are ready to visit. For an ordinary user, Maps costs Google a few rupees a year to serve but makes them more likely to use Google Search and click local ads.

howTheyGetUsers: Pre-installed on almost every Android phone
Search results that open in Maps
Android Auto, CarPlay and cars with Google built in
Shared links in WhatsApp for locations
whatBringsUsersBack: Looking up places and opening hours
growth.moat: Maps has a data network effect: billions of users give live traffic, reviews and edits, which make Maps better, which brings more users. Rivals can buy satellite images but not this constant stream of fresh data. Being pre-installed on Android adds a distribution moat.

competitors.name: Apple Maps
competitors.positioning: Default map on iPhones, strong privacy message.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Google Maps has more place data and reviews, and works on all phones.

competitors.name: Mappls (MapmyIndia)
competitors.positioning: Indian map app with detailed Indian road data, speed bump and pothole alerts.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Google has many more users and reviews; Mappls has deeper Indian road detail and government support.

competitors.name: Ola Maps
competitors.positioning: Ola's map platform, cheaper APIs for Indian developers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Google has better global coverage; Ola competes on API price.

competitors.name: Waze
competitors.positioning: Community driving app, also owned by Google.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Maps covers all transport and places; Waze focuses on drivers.

competitors.name: AI assistants like ChatGPT
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Maps has live data, reviews and navigation built in.

pmLessons: User contributions can be a moat: every review and traffic signal makes the product better.
Free products still need a money plan; Maps earns through local ads and APIs, not from users.
In new markets, local details like flyovers and two-wheelers decide trust.
Safety failures in the real world hurt a digital product's trust far more than small bugs.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve Google Maps for two-wheeler riders in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona, top pains (narrow lanes, rain, parking), ideas, metric like completed trips per rider.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Google Maps make more money without annoying users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Local ads, Ask Maps sponsored results, bookings. Guardrails on trust and relevance.

interviewQuestions.question: Measure the success of Ask Maps.
interviewQuestions.hint: Adoption, queries per user, actions taken, repeat use, accuracy. Compare against normal search.

interviewQuestions.question: A news story says Maps led a car to an unfinished bridge. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Immediate fix, root cause (data freshness), process with local authorities, metrics to track.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Google Maps' north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Trips and visits completed. Break into navigation, discovery, data freshness, business participation.
